claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has a single-phase BCC structure.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density.
The baseline alloy has insufficient room-temperature ductility.
Adding 2-5 at.% Al can trigger B2 ordering while retaining a BCC matrix.
Al addition will precipitate a B2-ordered intermetallic phase of NiAl-type or HfAl-type in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The B2 phase will form a continuous or semi-continuous reticulated network along grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
The B2 network will bridge and deflect cracks and increase the energy required for crack propagation.
The BCC matrix will provide ductility in the proposed dual-phase microstructure.
Dual-phase high-entropy alloys can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
Simple solid-solution hardening typically reduces ductility.
The Al-modified alloy will have greater yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will have greater ultimate tensile strength than the baseline alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will have greater uniform elongation than the baseline alloy.
The strength gain will proportionally exceed any density increase, producing improved specific strength.
The baseline alloy's low ductility is caused by limited room-temperature slip systems and the absence of crack-bridging mechanisms.
A fully continuous intermetallic skeleton formed above an Al-content threshold would be brittle and cause catastrophic failure.
BCC alloys are typically brittle during room-temperature compression.
Annealing will promote phase separation and reticulated-network formation in the Al-modified alloy.
Al is less dense than the principal elements of the baseline refractory alloy.
A decrease in ductility after Al addition would indicate either solid-solution hardening or formation of a brittle phase without effective network bridging.

contradictions.description: The operating regime and experiment specify uniaxial compression, but the predicted outcome invokes ultimate tensile strength and uniform elongation, which are tensile-test metrics and cannot be obtained from the proposed compression curves.

The predicted outcome asserts a net density increase, whereas the uncertainty field says the density trade-off is unresolved and emphasizes that Al is lighter. The direction of the density change is therefore stated inconsistently.
